passage:
Monday: In the corridor, two classmates made a joke about Sharmila's skin, loud enough for the whole row to hear. Her cheeks burned and she looked at the floor.
Wednesday: The joke came back with a new nickname. This time she took a breath, said nothing, and walked to Minakshi's bench. She didn't laugh along and she didn't snap; there was nothing for them to feed on. They lost interest by lunch.
The next Tuesday: When it happened again, she had written down the dates, and she took them to the class teacher, who spoke to the two students. Minakshi sat with her in the canteen. Sharmila thought, nobody else gets a vote on what I'm worth.

qa.q: What did Sharmila do with the dates she had written down?
qa.a: She took them to the class teacher.

qa.q: What was Sharmila feeling in the corridor, and how do you know?
qa.a: Her cheeks burned and she looked at the floor, which shows embarrassment and hurt.

qa.q: Why did ignoring the joke, and later reporting it, work?
qa.a: Not reacting gave them nothing to feed on, and when it happened again, the written dates let a teacher step in.

qa.q: How might Minakshi's company have mattered to Sharmila?
qa.a: Sitting with her in the canteen and offering a bench to walk to told Sharmila she belonged and wasn't alone.

grounding: Shows a teen mocked about her skin, ignoring it, recording dates, telling a teacher, and keeping her worth her own.

passage: It started in Class 9, when I was still the shortest in our section. 'Oye, Shankar, stand on the bench so we can see you!' Every morning someone had a new line, and every morning I laughed along or snapped back, which only gave them more to play with. Looking back, the change came from something small. One day I just didn't react. I kept copying the board. It went quiet faster than I expected. But two of them kept going, leaving a toy ladder on my desk every day for a week, so I finally told Sangeeta Ma'am after chemistry. She listened, said it was not my fault, moved those two to the front bench that same afternoon and called their parents. What I remember most is what she said at the door: 'Your worth isn't decided by a class vote, Shankar.' I'm still short. I've stopped thinking that's a problem.

qa.q: What did two classmates leave on Shankar's desk?
qa.a: They left a toy ladder on the desk every day for a week.

qa.q: What was Shankar probably feeling while laughing along every morning?
qa.a: Shankar laughed along or snapped back every morning, which suggests feeling hurt and embarrassed while trying to hide it.
Not reacting took the fun away for most of them, and telling Sangeeta Ma'am when it kept going got an adult to stop it.

qa.q: How does Sangeeta Ma'am see the teasing?
qa.a: She sees it as repeated mockery that needs action, not a joke, so she moves the two and calls their parents.

grounding: A first-person look back at being mocked for height, learning not to feed it, telling a teacher when it repeated, and that worth is not decided by others.

passage: PE teacher's note, 14 August. During warm-up I heard Shalini's group call Bhavna 'pimple map' again while she tied her laces. This is the third time this month I've heard something about her skin or her weight. Bhavna didn't turn round. She finished her laces, jogged to the front and kept her eyes on the cones, though her ears had gone red. After class she came to me with a friend and asked, very quietly, if I could make it stop, because it happens in the corridor too. I thanked her for telling me and said none of it had anything to do with her worth. I spoke to Shalini's group before the next bell, recorded it, and passed it to the class teacher, Mr D'Souza, who phoned their parents that afternoon. I will keep a close eye on warm-ups and corridors.

qa.q: What did Shalini's group call Bhavna?
qa.a: They called her 'pimple map' during warm-up.

qa.q: What do Bhavna's red ears suggest while she kept her eyes on the cones?
qa.a: They suggest she felt embarrassed and hurt, even though she chose not to react.
She didn't feed the jokes in the moment, then told a teacher once it kept happening, so an adult could stop it.

qa.q: How might Shalini's group see the joke?
qa.a: They may treat it as harmless fun, not noticing how it hurts Bhavna or that it says more about them than her.

grounding: A teacher's note showing a teen mocked about her skin and weight who ignores it, avoids feeding it and tells a teacher when it repeats.
